title: Enhancement: Support BMC Platforms EEPROM without a Base MAC TLV in chassis API tests
author: norimeher-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the enhancement

The chassis platform API test 
`[tests/platform_tests/api/test_chassis.py::TestChassisApi::test_get_system_eeprom_info] `

assume that every system EEPROM contains an ONIE Base MAC Address TLV.

In a BMC test environment, the chassis API reads the BMC EEPROM rather than the host CPU EEPROM. The Goldfinch BMC EEPROM does not contain a Base MAC TLV because the BMC management MAC is instead derived from the host CPU EEPROM’s MAC address using a platform-defined offset. Therefore, the test fails even though the returned BMC EEPROM data is valid for this platform.

This is a platform-specific test gap, not an EEPROM or platform API failure.

### Steps to Reproduce

1) Run the chassis platform API test on arm64-arista_goldfinch-r0
           `tests/platform_tests/api/test_chassis.py::TestChassisApi::test_get_system_eeprom_info`
2) Observe the system EEPROM validation failure due to the missing Base MAC TLV.

### Current Behavior

The test requires the Base MAC TLV and attempts to validate it, causing the chassis API test to fail on Goldfinch BMC.

### Proposed Behavior

For Goldfinch BMC, the test should not require or validate the Base MAC TLV because it is not present in the BMC EEPROM.

All other required EEPROM fields should remain validated, and platforms expected to provide a Base MAC TLV should continue using the existing validation.
